title: Tapestry Attributor: streaming aggregator for per-route/model/customer cost & latency breakdowns
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The Console needs a single, low-latency streaming service that produces authoritative per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns that match (or explain) the billing ledger and the latency SLO dashboards. Current batch rollups are slow to surface regressions and miss attribution details from batching, KV cache hits, and model-variant fallbacks.

Goal: Implement the 'Tapestry Attributor' — a streaming aggregation pipeline and lightweight enrichment service that: 1) consumes runtime telemetry (request traces, kernel telemetry, batching metadata, KV cache events), 2) incrementally computes attribution for cost (per-token, model-kernel cost, GPU-second apportionment) and latency (queue time, execution time, tail latencies), and 3) writes normalized per-minute per-(route, model_version, customer) rows for Console dashboards, alerts, and the chargeback reconciler.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace the canonical billing ledger export; it provides the analytical, explainable breakdown used by Console and ops. The authoritative final bill will remain the billing pipeline but should reconcile within a small tolerance.
acceptance_criteria: Stream consumer reads runtime telemetry from Kafka topic 'runtime-telemetry-v2' and handles 99th percentile event lateness up to 5m without data loss.

Produces per-minute records (partitioned by customer, route, model_version) including fields: tokens_in, tokens_out, effective_gpu_ms, batch_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, compute_cost_usd, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, attribution_signals (stringified explanation).
Aggregations reconcile against the daily billing ledger within 0.5% for high-volume tenants and within 2% for low-volume tenants after a 24-hour window.
Console dashboards can query the output table with <500ms median query latency for a single-customer one-hour slice (ClickHouse target).
End-to-end tests (integration) exist that inject synthetic traces with batching and KV cache scenarios and assert correct apportionment and stable incremental updates.
implementation_notes: Ingress: Kafka topics with keys (request_id) and envelope that includes trace_id, route_id, model_tag, customer_id, kernel_profile, tokens_requested, tokens_returned, batch_id (optional), cache_hit boolean, timestamp.

Processing: Apache Flink job (state backend = RocksDB) to do per-request enrichment (attach model cost profile from config store), then windowed incremental apportionment into per-minute shards. Use event-time processing with watermarking and allowed lateness=5m.

State: Keep lightweight running counts per (customer, route, model_version, minute) and last-seen kernel_profile signatures to compute GPU-ms estimates; persist checkpoints to S3 (or GCS) for recovery.

Enrichment: Periodic join against Config DB (consul/kv or config service) to pull per-model token-cost, kernel-cost factors, and quantization multipliers. Fall back to default profiles when missing and emit a 'profile_missing' label.

Output: Write per-minute rows to ClickHouse for fast Console reads and to Parquet on S3 (analytics) for longer-term reconciliations. Also publish summarized deltas to 'attributor-deltas' topic for downstream consumers (alerts, chargeback).
Correctness: Include idempotency keys per request_id so reprocessed events don't double-count. Use compaction for late-arriving updates (last-write-wins on event timestamp).

Operational: Expose metrics: processed_events_total, processing_lag_seconds_p50/p95/p99, upstream_late_events, state_size_bytes, checkpoint_age. Add alerting runbooks for high-latency or state growth anomalies.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14 - Ticket created by Ava. Initial scope drafted after sync with Console PMs (Lina Patel).

2025-02-18 - Design review: agreed on Flink + ClickHouse + Parquet outputs. Marcus sketched state layout and idempotency plan. Action: engineering spike to validate RocksDB state size with synthetic high-cardinality tenants.

2025-02-24 - Spike results: 3M active minute-shards for largest tenant estimated -> need tiered compaction and TTL. Decided to add per-tenant sampling for detailed historical retention to limit storage growth.
2025-02-27 - Implemented parser for 'runtime-telemetry-v2' and local Flink job harness. Parser handles both new and legacy trace envelopes. Unit tests added for KV cache attribution logic.

2025-03-02 - End-to-end staging run with 24h of replays: produced ClickHouse schema and initial rows. Reconciled gross compute_cost to billing simulator: 0.9% delta for synthetic high-volume workload. Next: harden watermarking and late data reconciliation logic.
